messages:
Amy Chen: Quick question — I'm starting parental leave on 2025-04-10 and we'll be in the UK for ~8 weeks to help with family. I need to put down a childcare deposit for an August start. Does Redwood reimburse childcare deposits paid to a non-US provider?

Ravi Patel: congrats Amy! I think deposits can be reimbursed if they meet the "eligible childcare expense" rules, but international vendors sometimes need extra paperwork. cc @Jordan (People Ops)

Jordan (People Ops): Short answer: yes, we can reimburse eligible childcare deposits paid abroad, but there are extra steps. Will outline what we need.

Jordan (People Ops): For reimbursement, please submit these items via Expensify and tag "parental-leave-childcare":
```
- Vendor invoice/contract showing deposit amount and refund terms
- Proof of payment (bank transfer receipt, card statement, or provider confirmation)
- Copy of the childcare provider's contact info and address
- English translation of invoice if not in English (one-paragraph OK)
- Short note stating intended childcare dates and child name/age
```

Jordan (People Ops): Additional notes for international cases:
- Convert the reimbursed amount to USD using the exchange rate on date of payment and attach the source (xe.com, bank rate screenshot, or card statement).
- If deposit is refundable, we treat it like any other expense; if refunded later, you must return refund to Redwood (we'll provide a simple refund flow).

Emma (Finance): For non-US payments we need the provider's bank details if you'd prefer Redwood to pay the vendor directly. Otherwise we reimburse you in USD after conversion. If the provider requests payment to a business account, Finance may ask for a supplier form.

PayrollBot: Heads-up: depending on country and payment structure, childcare reimbursements may be taxable or need to be processed through payroll. Finance will flag any tax implications and let you know.

Amy Chen: Thanks. Is there a filing deadline? I may not submit until mid-June when I have the final contract.

Jordan (People Ops): Please submit within 90 days of the payment to avoid delays. If you need an exception because of timing while on leave, DM me and we'll note it in the ticket.

Michelle Rivera: Also tagging benefits team — if you use a UK-registered provider while on short-term assignment, double-check whether local VAT rules or refunds apply. We won't handle VAT recovery.

Jordan (People Ops): Action items for Amy: 1) Save contract + proof of payment, 2) take screenshot of exchange rate/source, 3) submit via Expensify with tag and set policy to "Parental Leave - Childcare". I'll create a benefits ticket and link it to your HR file.

Amy Chen: Perfect, will do. Appreciate the clear checklist. I'll DM @Jordan with dates and the provider contact.

Benefits Bot: Ticket created: BENEFITS-8421 — "International childcare deposit reimbursement for Amy Chen". Jordan assigned.

Emma (Finance): Once you submit, give us 7-10 business days to process. If you want Redwood to pay the vendor directly, include the vendor banking details and a copy of the invoice.

Amy Chen: Great — sending docs now. Thanks everyone! :heart:
